subject: Government
title: Constitutions and Constitutionalism
outline: Meaning and purposes of a constitution

modules.title: Meaning, Sources and Purposes
modules.html:
A constitution is the body of fundamental rules — written or unwritten, legal and conventional — according to which a state is governed. It creates the organs of government, distributes powers among them, defines the relationship between government and citizen, and provides the procedure for its own amendment.

Sources of a constitution:

  • Statutes / Acts of parliament — e.g. the Magna Carta 1215, the Bill of Rights 1689.
  • Judicial precedent — decisions of superior courts interpreting the constitution.
  • Conventions — unwritten practices regarded as binding, e.g. that the British monarch assents to bills.
  • Customs and traditions of the people.
  • Constitutional conferences and commissions — e.g. the 1957–58 London and Lagos conferences.
  • Foreign constitutions and international treaties.
  • Historical documents and past constitutions.
  • Works of eminent jurists.

Purposes: to establish and limit government, guarantee fundamental rights, distribute powers between organs and levels, provide legitimacy and stability, and supply an orderly method of change.

examples.q: Give one Nigerian example of a convention.
examples.a: The practice of zoning the presidency between the North and the South, and the informal rotation of party offices, are political conventions: they are not written in the 1999 Constitution but are widely observed.

modules.title: Written and Unwritten Constitutions
modules.html:
BasisWritten constitutionUnwritten constitution
FormProvisions assembled in a single formal document.Scattered across statutes, conventions, precedents and treatises.
OriginUsually the product of a deliberate act – a convention or assembly.Grows gradually over centuries.
ExamplesNigeria (1999), USA (1787), India.United Kingdom, Israel, New Zealand.
AmendmentNormally rigid, needing a special procedure.Normally flexible; ordinary legislation suffices.
MeritsClarity, certainty, safeguard for rights, suitable for federations.Flexible, adaptable, avoids deadlock.
DemeritsMay be rigid and outdated; legalistic disputes.Uncertain, unsuitable for federations, weak protection for minorities.

Note carefully: no constitution is wholly written or wholly unwritten. Nigeria's written constitution operates alongside unwritten conventions; Britain's unwritten constitution includes many written statutes.

examples.q: Why is a written constitution regarded as essential in a federation?
examples.a: Because the division of powers between the central and component governments must be clear, certain and beyond unilateral alteration; only a written, entrenched document can guarantee that.

modules.title: Rigid and Flexible Constitutions
modules.html:
A rigid constitution is one that can only be amended by a special, difficult procedure — a special majority, approval by component units, or a referendum. A flexible constitution can be amended by the ordinary law-making process.

Nigeria's 1999 Constitution is rigid. Under section 9, an ordinary amendment requires:

  1. A resolution supported by at least two-thirds majority of all the members of each House of the National Assembly; and
  2. Approval by resolution of the Houses of Assembly of not less than two-thirds of all the 36 states.

Amendments touching sections 8 (creation of states), 9 (the amendment procedure itself) and Chapter IV (fundamental rights) require a four-fifths majority of all members of each House of the National Assembly, plus the two-thirds of state assemblies.

Merits of rigidity: stability, protection of minorities and rights, prevention of hasty change, safeguard of the federal bargain. Demerits: difficulty of adapting to new needs; may provoke extra-constitutional change such as coups.

examples.q: Which majority is required to alter the fundamental rights chapter of the 1999 Constitution?
examples.a: A four-fifths majority of all the members of each House of the National Assembly, together with the approval of at least two-thirds of the 36 state Houses of Assembly.

modules.title: Constitutionalism
modules.html:
Constitutionalism is the doctrine that government must be conducted according to, and limited by, the constitution. The mere existence of a constitution is not enough; constitutionalism requires that it be obeyed. As the saying goes, “every state has a constitution, but not every state practises constitutionalism.”

Features of constitutionalism:

  • Supremacy of the constitution — section 1(1) and 1(3) of the 1999 Constitution declare it supreme and void any inconsistent law.
  • Rule of law and equality before the law.
  • Separation of powers with checks and balances.
  • Independent judiciary and judicial review.
  • Guaranteed fundamental human rights.
  • Periodic free elections and limited tenure.
  • Accountability and transparency in government.

Obstacles in Nigeria: military interventions that suspended constitutions, executive lawlessness and disobedience of court orders, abuse of emergency powers, corruption, ethnic pressures and weak institutions.

examples.q: A state governor refuses to obey a valid court judgment. Which principle is violated?
examples.a: Constitutionalism, and specifically the rule of law: government must act within the law and submit to the decisions of the courts.

modules.title: Unitary, federal and confederal constitutions
modules.html:
Unitary, federal and confederal constitutions is a key part of Constitutions and Constitutionalism (SSS 1, Government). Master the meaning, the main points and how it is tested in JAMB and WAEC questions on this topic.

Key points

  • Foreign constitutions and international treaties.
  • Historical documents and past constitutions.
  • Merits of rigidity: stability, protection of minorities and rights, prevention of hasty change, safeguard of the federal bargain.
  • Obstacles in Nigeria: military interventions that suspended constitutions, executive lawlessness and disobedience of court orders, abuse of emergency powers, corruption, ethnic pressures and weak institutions.
  • The federal bargain must be entrenched.

Worked example

Q: A federation requires a constitution that is
A: Written and rigid — The federal bargain must be entrenched.

Q: Which statement is TRUE?
A: No constitution is wholly written or wholly unwritten — All constitutions mix written and unwritten elements.

quiz.q: A constitution is best defined as
options: A book of laws for criminals
The body of fundamental rules by which a state is governed
quiz.solution: It is the fundamental law establishing and limiting government.

quiz.q: Which country operates an unwritten constitution?
quiz.solution: Britain's constitution is scattered and largely conventional.

quiz.q: A rigid constitution is one that
options: Requires a special procedure to amend
quiz.solution: Rigidity refers to a special amendment procedure.

quiz.q: Section 9 of the 1999 Constitution deals with
quiz.solution: It prescribes the amendment procedure.

quiz.q: Ordinary amendment of the 1999 Constitution requires the approval of
options: A simple majority of the National Assembly
Two-thirds of each House plus two-thirds of state assemblies
quiz.solution: That is the section 9(2) requirement.

quiz.q: Which is NOT a source of a constitution?
quiz.solution: Weather has no bearing on constitutional sources.

quiz.q: Conventions are
quiz.solution: They are customary practices accepted as obligatory.

quiz.q: Constitutionalism means
options: Government limited by and conducted according to the constitution
quiz.solution: It is limited government under the constitution.

quiz.q: Supremacy of the Nigerian constitution is declared in
quiz.solution: Section 1(1) and 1(3) establish supremacy.

quiz.q: A merit of a written constitution is
quiz.solution: The rules are stated clearly in one document.

quiz.q: A federation requires a constitution that is
quiz.solution: The federal bargain must be entrenched.

quiz.q: The Magna Carta of 1215 is a source of the constitution of
quiz.solution: It is a foundational British constitutional document.

quiz.q: Judicial review is best protected by
quiz.solution: Only an independent judiciary can check other organs.

quiz.q: Amendment of Chapter IV of the 1999 Constitution requires
options: Four-fifths majority of each House plus two-thirds of states
quiz.solution: Fundamental rights are specially entrenched.

quiz.q: A demerit of a rigid constitution is that it
options: May be difficult to adapt to change
quiz.solution: Rigidity can frustrate needed reform.

quiz.q: Which statement is TRUE?
options: No constitution is wholly written or wholly unwritten
quiz.solution: All constitutions mix written and unwritten elements.

quiz.q: An unwritten constitution is one that is _____.
options: totally in the memory of the elders
quiz.solution: An unwritten constitution, like that of the UK, is not found in a single document but consists of a collection of laws, judicial precedents, customs, and conventions.

quiz.q: An advantage of a flexible constitution is that _____.
options: it can be easily adapted to emergencies
it is always in a single document
quiz.solution: A flexible constitution (like the UK's) can be amended by a simple majority in parliament, making it easier to change in response to urgent national needs.

quiz.q: Which of the following is a feature of a rigid constitution?
options: It can be amended by a simple majority
It requires a special and difficult amendment process
It is found in a unitary state
quiz.solution: A rigid constitution (like Nigeria's or the USA's) requires a complex legal procedure, such as a two-thirds majority in the legislature, to be amended.

quiz.q: A written constitution is often _____, making it hard to change.
quiz.solution: Most written constitutions are rigid because they require specific, difficult procedures for amendment.

quiz.q: Which of the following is a feature of a written constitution?
quiz.solution: Past question (WAEC 2025). Correct answer: It is rigid.

quiz.q: The constitutional tenure of a Nigerian President is?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: 4 years.

quiz.q: The Lyttleton Constitution of 1954 was significant because it _____.
options: introduced the office of the Prime Minister
quiz.solution: The 1954 Lyttleton Constitution formally established Nigeria as a federation by sharing powers between the central government and the regional governments.

quiz.q: The 1979 Constitution of Nigeria introduced the _____.
quiz.solution: The 1979 Constitution marked a shift from the British-style parliamentary system to the American-style presidential system, with an executive President.

quiz.q: The 1963 Constitution of Nigeria replaced the _____.
options: Queen of England as Head of State
Prime Minister as Head of Government
Federal system with a unitary one
quiz.solution: The 1963 Republican Constitution abolished the monarchy in Nigeria, replacing the Queen with an indigenous President as the Head of State.

quiz.q: A major feature of the Macpherson Constitution of 1951 was the _____.
quiz.solution: The 1951 Macpherson Constitution introduced a semi-responsible government by creating central and regional legislatures with appointed ministers.

quiz.q: The Richard's Constitution of 1946 was noted for dividing Nigeria into _____.
quiz.solution: The Richard's Constitution divided Nigeria into three administrative regions: Northern, Western, and Eastern regions.

quiz.q: The 1999 Constitution of Nigeria is _____.
quiz.solution: A rigid constitution requires a special, difficult procedure for amendment. The 1999 Nigerian Constitution requires 2/3 majority of both chambers and 2/3 of State Assemblies.

quiz.q: Who was the Chairman of the 1976 Constitution Drafting Committee in Nigeria?
quiz.solution: Chief Rotimi Williams headed the '49 Wise Men' committee that drafted the 1979 Constitution.

quiz.q: A major criticism of the 1922 Clifford Constitution was that _____.
options: it excluded the North from the Legislative Council
it gave too much power to Nigerians
quiz.solution: The Legislative Council under Clifford only made laws for the Southern Province, while the Governor continued to rule the North by proclamation.

quiz.q: Which of the following is a source of a constitution?
quiz.solution: Judicial precedents (past court rulings) are a vital source of constitutional law, especially in common law systems.

quiz.q: The 1989 Constitution of Nigeria was never fully implemented because _____.
options: it was rejected by the people
quiz.solution: The 1989 Constitution was designed for the Third Republic, which was cut short by the annulment of the June 12, 1993, presidential election.

quiz.q: Who was the first Nigerian to be appointed as a Minister in the colonial era?
quiz.solution: Ministerial appointments for Nigerians only began under the 1951 Macpherson Constitution. Note: Question difficulty is High; early ministers included various regional leaders.

quiz.q: The 1951 Macpherson Constitution was criticized for being _____.
quiz.solution: It was described as a compromise because it tried to satisfy both the centralist and regionalist demands of Nigerian politicians.

quiz.q: Which pre-colonial Nigerian political system was described as acephalous?
quiz.solution: 'Acephalous' means headless. The Igbo traditional political system was decentralized and lacked a single central authority or king.

quiz.q: The highest court of appeal in Nigeria under the 1999 Constitution is the _____.
quiz.solution: The Supreme Court of Nigeria is the final appellate court and the highest judicial body in the country.

quiz.q: The 'Elective Principle' was first introduced in Nigeria by the _____ Constitution.
quiz.solution: The 1922 Clifford Constitution introduced the elective principle, allowing for the first time the election of representatives into the Legislative Council.

quiz.q: The Richards Constitution of 1946 was significant because it _____.
options: Divided Nigeria into three administrative regions
quiz.solution: The Richards Constitution formally divided Nigeria into the Northern, Western, and Eastern regions, laying the foundation for regionalism.

quiz.q: The Macpherson Constitution of 1951 was criticized for being _____.
quiz.solution: It was described as a compromise because it attempted to balance the demands for central authority and regional autonomy.

quiz.q: The main reason for the failure of the 1922 Clifford Constitution was that _____.
options: It excluded Northern Nigeria from the Legislative Council
It gave too much power to Nigerians
quiz.solution: The Clifford Constitution only legislated for the Southern Protectorate, while the North was ruled by proclamations of the Governor.

quiz.q: The 1999 Constitution of Nigeria provides for _____ states.
quiz.solution: Nigeria currently has 36 states and a Federal Capital Territory (Abuja) as established in the 1999 Constitution.

quiz.q: The first Nigerian Prime Minister was _____.
quiz.solution: Sir Abubakar Tafawa Balewa was the Prime Minister of Nigeria from 1957 until his assassination in 1966.

quiz.q: The Lyttleton Constitution of 1954 made Nigeria a _____.
quiz.solution: The Lyttleton Constitution formally established the federal principle by dividing powers between the center and the regions.

quiz.q: The term of office for a member of the Nigerian Senate is _____ years.
quiz.solution: Members of both the Senate and the House of Representatives in Nigeria serve 4-year terms.

quiz.q: Who was the Chairman of the 1976 Constitution Drafting Committee?
quiz.solution: Chief Rotimi Williams headed the '49 Wise Men' committee that drafted the 1979 Constitution.

quiz.q: The 1989 Constitution of Nigeria was intended for the _____.
quiz.solution: The 1989 Constitution was designed for the transition to the Third Republic, which was aborted following the annulment of the June 12, 1993 election.

quiz.q: The 1979 Constitution introduced the:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2021). Correct answer: Presidential system.

quiz.q: The Lyttelton Constitution of 1954 established:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2021). Correct answer: Federalism.

quiz.q: The Richards Constitution divided Nigeria into:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2021). Correct answer: 3 Regions.

quiz.q: A constitution that is easy to amend is:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2021). Correct answer: Flexible.
